portfolio.title: Investment Club Portfolio
portfolio.subtitle: Stock Picks, Holdings Review & Recommendations
portfolio.week_narrative: Markets recovered strongly this week with the S&P 500 up 1.73% and Nasdaq surging 2.65%, capping an April that saw the S&P gain over 10% — its best monthly performance since November 2020. The week was not without turbulence: mid-week oil price spikes tied to U.S.-Iran tensions briefly sent the Dow down 550 points before a pullback in oil prices sparked a sharp recovery. The Fed held rates steady at 3.5–3.75% in what became a historically contentious 8-4 vote — the most dissent since 1992 — signaling growing internal disagreement about the path forward. Earnings were a mixed bag: AMD and Caterpillar beat estimates decisively, while Netflix missed Q2 guidance and Meta shed nearly 10% on AI investment headwinds and a 10% workforce cut.

holdings.name: Strategy Inc
holdings.rationale: Massive 18% week driven by Bitcoin momentum. Well below 52-week high of $457 — long-term thesis intact. Take no action; let the Bitcoin cycle play out but do not chase at this level.

holdings.name: Netflix, Inc.
holdings.rationale: Q2 guidance miss and Reed Hastings’ board exit spooked the market. However, Netflix approved a $25B buyback — signaling deep confidence from the board. Price is approaching 52-week low support at $75. Hold and monitor.

holdings.name: NVIDIA Corporation
holdings.rationale: Down 6% on OpenAI revenue miss concerns, but Micron’s HBM chips are sold out through 2026 — confirming AI infrastructure demand is real. NVDA earnings are May 27. 37 analysts rate Strong Buy with a $270 target. This dip is an opportunity.

holdings.name: Vanguard S&P 500 ETF
holdings.rationale: Near its 52-week high of $666.55 after April’s historic monthly rally. Core long-term position. Continue dollar-cost averaging. No action needed.

watchlist.name: Microsoft Corporation
watchlist.rationale: Down 3% alongside broader tech weakness. Azure cloud growth remains the core thesis. Sitting 26% below its 52-week high of $555. Watch for stabilization near $400 as a potential entry point.

watchlist.name: Meta Platforms, Inc.
watchlist.rationale: Nearly -10% this week — the week’s biggest loser. 10% global workforce cut announced to offset AI investment costs. Short-term pain, but leaner operations could drive margin expansion. Watch for a base near $580–590 before considering entry.

watchlist.name: Invesco QQQ Trust
watchlist.rationale: Near its all-time high. Broad tech ETF strength confirms the Nasdaq rally has legs beyond individual names. A good benchmark for gauging tech sector health.

watchlist.name: SPDR Dow Jones ETF
watchlist.rationale: Steady near 52-week highs. Caterpillar’s +10% earnings pop drove industrial component strength. Defensive but growing — watch for any break above $505 all-time high.

key_insights: MSTR +18% and NVDA -6% in the same week shows crypto/AI divergence is real right now
Fed’s 8-4 rate hold vote is the most contested since 1992 — policy uncertainty is elevated
April’s S&P +10% month is historic — stay invested but tighten stop-losses heading into summer

side_income.title: Side Income & Business Moves
side_income.subtitle: Specific Opportunities This Week

opportunities.name: High-Yield Savings Account (HYSA)
opportunities.how_to_start: Open Marcus by Goldman Sachs or Ally Bank online in 10 minutes. Move idle checking cash immediately. Fed holding rates means these rates stay elevated through at least year-end.

opportunities.name: U.S. Treasury Bills (4-Week or 13-Week)
opportunities.how_to_start: Open a free TreasuryDirect.gov account. Purchase at the next weekly auction. Minimum $100. Given the Fed’s hold and elevated inflation, locking in T-bill rates now is smart.

opportunities.name: META Dip Play — Covered Opportunity
opportunities.potential_return: 15–25% upside if thesis plays out in 6–12 months
opportunities.how_to_start: META is down nearly 10% this week and 24% off its 52-week high. The 10% workforce cut will compress costs and expand margins. Watch for stabilization near $580–590 and evaluate a small position if the club thesis supports it.

opportunities.name: NVDA Pre-Earnings Positioning
opportunities.how_to_start: NVDA reports earnings May 27. Micron’s HBM sold-out status confirms AI chip demand is real. Consider a small position now or a defined-risk options play before the earnings catalyst. Do not over-allocate before earnings.

news_hooks.event: Fed holds rates at 3.5–3.75% in historically split 8-4 vote
news_hooks.opportunity: Rates staying elevated longer than expected — HYSA and T-bills still paying meaningfully above inflation
news_hooks.action: Move any cash sitting in a standard checking account into a HYSA or T-bill this week

news_hooks.opportunity: Airline consolidation means fewer budget options — legacy carriers (DAL, UAL) and their investors benefit
news_hooks.action: Add DAL or UAL to the watchlist as a potential beneficiary of reduced low-cost competition

news_hooks.opportunity: Layoffs signal cost discipline — margin expansion likely in Q3/Q4 2026 earnings
news_hooks.action: Put META on the watchlist at $580 support and revisit after Q2 earnings

key_insights: T-bills at ~5% with the Fed on hold — idle cash is losing value if not deployed here
NVDA’s -6% dip ahead of May 27 earnings is a historically favorable setup
META’s workforce cut is short-term pain hiding long-term margin expansion
